To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
light fermions dilute the chromomagnetic condensate, making it less efficient for confinement.

the confinement transition in lattice QCD-like theories with N(f)~N(c) is at significantly stronger coupling than the one in the N(f)=N(c)=0 limit, and that light fermions can dilute chromomagnetic monoples, via zero modes.
light fermions dilute the chromomagnetic condensate, and this is a mechanism of confinement in QCD-like gauge theories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between confinement and chiral dynamics in strongly interacting matter.
the mechanism of confinement in QCD and its relation to the properties of the quark-gluon plasma at high temperature.
the confinement transition in gauge theories with a large number of fermionic flavors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a light fermion number of order N(f)~1000 is required for a Bose-Einstein condensate of chromomagnetic monoples to form, which in turn leads to confinement.
the light quarks are the main source of monopole condensation and confinement in QCD.
the mechanism of confinement is the Bose-Einstein condensate of the chromomagnetic fluxtubes, and the confinement transition is the condensation transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanism of confinement is not the condensation of monopoles, but rather their Bose-Einstein condensate-like occupation by light quarks.
the confinement transition in the N(f)~N(c) QCD-like theories is driven by the Bose-Einstein condensate of chromomagnetic monpoles.
the light fermions, via the zero modes on the monopoles, make the latter distinguishable and hence unsuitable for condensation, which is a prerequisite of confinement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

light fermions can affect the confinement transition in ways that are difficult to capture in the effective theory of monopole condensation.  ( +info ) The chiral phase transition and the electroweak phase transition in QCD with many quark flavors.
